subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB488 LANDED. SR11 and 13.16.3 SR24 e) state the SAME prohibition from two directions -- SR11 speaks of the conditional variable's class, SR24 e) of the entry a condition-name may be associated with -- so they are enforced by ONE screen and the COBOL1976 message quotes both. The class question is resolved through 13.18.60.3 SR4's own predicate rather than a second hand-written class list: SR4 names 'The INDEX, MESSAGE-TAG, OBJECT REFERENCE, POINTER, FUNCTION-POINTER, and PROGRAM-POINTER phrases', which are exactly the six USAGE phrases producing SR11's four classes (8.5.2), and a unit drift test asserts the two populations are the same set for every Usage member. The WRITTEN clause is read alongside the resolved PicInfo because a MESSAGE-TAG entry is refused non-support at ParseUsage (COBOL1943) and a FUNCTION-POINTER entry is staged there, so neither gains a PicInfo and only DataItem.OwnUsage sees them. BEFORE: the three classes failed three different ways -- class INDEX was accepted AND FULLY FUNCTIONAL (`01 IX USAGE INDEX. 88 C VALUE 1.` with `SET IX TO 1` took the TRUE branch at all four editions, a working nonconforming feature), while class POINTER and class OBJECT were accepted by the binder and then leaked a RAW ROSLYN ERROR the user could not act on (`if ((P == NULLL))` in the generated C#, `error CS0103: The name 'NULLL' does not exist in the current context`). Class message-tag stays unreachable because the usage itself is declined by name, which is why the screen's message-tag arm is exercised by the drift test rather than by a golden.  || CODE-LOCATION RE-POINTED 2026-09-13 (kb/Work PB391), verdict and evidence unchanged: the predicate that used to be `DataBinder.ConditionName#ExcludedConditionalVariableClass` is now `ItemCategory.IsIndexMessageTagObjectOrPointer`. It moved because a THIRD rule names the same four classes in the same words -- 14.7.6 rule 4's CORRESPONDING exclusion -- and its asker, CorrespondingBinder, is outside DataBinder; 13.18.60.3 SR4's and SR14's phrase readers moved with it, so the population is still stated once. SR24 e)'s row now calls the same member, and ConditionNameAssociationDriftTests.ExclusionEIsExactlySr4sUsagePopulation still asserts the two populations are one set.
